quest.title: The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil
quest.description: According to Citlali's plan, today's the day to guide Leyla's spirit back to his body. But will everything go off without a hitch...?
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Incense Ashcrystals x80, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Greetings again, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali, you're here!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I got the ceremonial sword from the chief. It has a certain power that's needed in situations like this.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...You haven't forgotten what we're doing today, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course not, we're gonna wake Leyla up! ...And then ask him just what the heck he was playing at.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: And I've prepared the rest of the tools for the ceremony, per Granny's instructions. We've dotted all our i's and crossed all our t's, so today should go off without a hitch.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Good work, kiddo. Then without further ado, let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Citlali summons the ceremonial sword "Calamity of Eshu."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I give offerings from the mystic smoke: The gift of stars on a moonless night, a wreath of dreams in the swirling wind.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Glory be to the Ruler of Death. Fade. Fade. Fade. Thrice uttered, and thrice repeated.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Is this one of her magic spells? This whole place suddenly got cold! What's happening!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Keep your voice down. We mustn't disturb her.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: We, the children of the priest-king, swear to abide by the ancient pact, and tear through the veil of the Night Realm.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I am Citlali, hear my command. I am the shepherd of doomsday, I am Ah K'ulbatil.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Look! Leyla's spirit is back. It's coming towards his body.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I shall pierce the cloak of night with flintstone, and banish all souls that do not belong to the land of the dead.\n

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Leyla! Obey my command, and return to the land where the sun shines. Return to your own path!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: D—Did it work?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Huh... Huh? Where am I? And... who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Whoa! ...G—Granny Itztli! I mean...! High Priestess Citlali! Please, have mercy!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Guilty conscience, huh? So you know full well what you've done.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea how close you were to never making it back? Or maybe you thought life would be more fun as an inanimate object?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I—I'm sorry! I messed up... and I'll face the consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh? You sure about that? Then say goodbye to your parents. Tell them this:

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: "Goodbye, Mom and Dad. I've realized I enjoy life as an empty shell so much that I've decided to get Granny Itztli to turn me into a stone statue, so I can stand guard over her house for the next hundred years."

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: No, please! Please don't, I'm begging you! I'll never do this again, I promise! Thank you, High Priestess Citlali, thank you for rescuing me!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't thank me — thank my grandson. If he hadn't sensed something was amiss, I wouldn't have bothered getting involved.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: You're more than welcome, Leyla. And don't mind Granny's — she's all bark and no bite. We're just glad that you're okay.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Besides, someone tricked you into doing this, didn't they? That Kokuchuu guy. He's the real culprit here.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: No... Mr. Kokuchuu had nothing to do with it. It was all my doing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Well, I mean, he suggested the method of using a powerful spirit relic as a medium. But it was my decision to go through with it. I wasn't coerced or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I'm the one to blame.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hah, the brainwashing is strong with this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... So, did Kokuchuu provide the relic?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: He did. He said it was a treasure related to the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, so that proves it — he was using you! He coaxed you into doing the clairvoyance for him!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: But I'm a spirit-duffer who can't cast a single spell... What use would I be to him?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Guys like me couldn't sense a spirit even if we spent the rest of our lives sitting and meditating.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: But Mr. Kokuchuu said that if I brute-force the spell and immerse myself in a spiritually rich substance, I might be able to catch a glimpse of one. Seemed like my only option...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, brute-forcing a spell when you're a spirit-duffer is like... forcing yourself to run a marathon without any legs! If it wasn't for Citlali, you'd have been lost forever!

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: I know, I'm sorry... It's just... everyone in this tribe is so amazingly talented, and then there's me... I just didn't wanna be the odd one out anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I totally understand how you feel, Leyla...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Some seeds effortlessly grow into beautiful cabbages, while others struggle with all their might and never even sprout.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Who knows why this is the way things are... Maybe that's just life? Life is full of things we can't change.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I know saying this doesn't change anything either, but I hope it makes you feel a little better.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Let's pause this discussion for now. We need to get you to Matla's for a checkup.

talks.objective: Head to where the witch doctor Matla is

dialogues.speaker: Matla
dialogues.text: Okay, looking good... Seems like this guy got off lightly. Just make sure he eats when you get back — he must be starving.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: That's a relief. I've heard of cases where people's bodies started necrotizing after they spent too long meditating.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a horrifying thought...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Mm. Anyway, Leyla, even though we didn't know each other before all this, I'm still really glad that you're okay now.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Well, maybe you didn't know me, but... I've heard all about you.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: #The same goes for High Priestess Citlali, {NICKNAME}, and Paimon. I've heard all the stories...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Even us?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: This might sound corny, but you're exactly the kind of people I've always dreamed of becoming... But it's clear to me now, that was just wishful thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Honestly, why'd I have to be born a spirit-duffer? Hehe, nah, it's alright really. I'm used to being useless by now. Thank you all for saving me.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Ororon, I think you're right — it's just a fact of life. I promise I won't take another risk like this in the future. I've brought you more than enough trouble already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, Leyla...

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Haha, it's okay! There's no need to comfort me.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, you little rascal. What are you talking about? Look at me.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Huh? What's wrong, High Priestess Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I said look at me. Take a good hard look. Sense anything strange?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Granny, what are YOU talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Another case of "happy to help" written on someone's face?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: ...Hold on, I think...

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: Either my mind's playing tricks on me, or... her entire body is an illusion.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: No... It must just be my imagination. I wouldn't be able to see through something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Wait, I know this trick... It's the same one I used a while back. Granny snuck away from right under our noses...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You see? You can perceive some spiritual abnormalities now. Congratulations.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: R—Really?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: But where are you going, Granny?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Where do you think? I'm going fishing, you dummy.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Someone triggered the trap I set in the cave. Looks like our friend Kokuchuu took the bait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Sorry, can't talk now. You'll find me in the cave.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (I don't believe it! He got away! Oh, this is terrible... Why'd I have to go and act so cocky about it? Ugh, I'm gonna look like such a fool...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (This Kokuchuu must be a real escape artist or something. But I can't tell them that. I'll have to think of something else...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali! Did you get him!?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Given that she's the only person here... I'm guessing no.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I thought I'd let him go. For now.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But I left a mark on him! So if he comes around here again, I'll be able to track his every move.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Oh, so Granny had only pretended to leave the cave... When in fact, she'd set up a whole trap for him and was lying in wait.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, so just like how you caught Ororon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how did you know Kokuchuu would come here?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Because I planted the bait here. The Mare Jivari map and the bow shard — left them both on the table. I had a feeling those were what he was truly after.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: And sure enough, my trap was triggered just moments after we left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you really did set up traps here after all, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Of course. It's just that they'd never do anything to either of you.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: See? What did I tell you?

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: So, Mr. Kokuchuu, you used me after all... This whole time, all you wanted was to find the location of the Mare Jivari.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's right. I've been wondering about the shard he left ever since I came across it. Why did he leave it there?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The moment I confirmed the Mare Jivari's location, that's when I realized: It was bait.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He was counting on Leyla's spirit getting lost, and the tribe coming to his rescue. Then, by helping Leyla, we'd be helping him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So he was fishing too! It was all a ploy to lure in an actual clairvoyant who could look into the shard for him...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yep. And somebody fell for it hook, line, and sinker...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. I took the bait...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: But so did Granny.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...! The nerve! I only got involved because of you, you little scamp!

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Either way, Kokuchuu played us like a fiddle. He managed to accomplish his goals without taking any of the risk himself. Pretty sneaky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You can say that again! Imagine if he'd tried to approach Citlali directly. She'd have seen through it right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Although, actually... Citlali, why did you let him go...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Uhhh... Because I couldn't risk using my full abilities here. He was a pretty slippery character, and if I'd kept him here by force, there could have been unintended consequences.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Was it my fault for picking a bad place...? I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I went looking for somewhere with a wealth of spiritual energy when I first decided to help Leyla, and ended up choosing this mad sage's hideout.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Mad sage?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Yeah, he's napping right behind that wall. We'd have a whole new situation on our hands if we woke him up. That's why I decided against using my full abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I do have some good news, though: I snatched the shard and map back before he bolted. So I may have restrained myself, but I certainly didn't let him walk all over me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's great! So he left empty-handed, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Uh, yes, sort of... The bad news is, he did get a look at the map before he left. Not that the Mare Jivari's last-known location is a huge secret, but still...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's kind of worrying... What if he's got some sorta diabolical plan?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll keep tracking him.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Also, Leyla — if it's all the same to you, I'd like to give the shard and map to {NICKNAME} as a gift. They might prove useful at some point in {M#his}{F#her} journey.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: #Absolutely! That's completely fine. {NICKNAME} deserves it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sure? This is a very generous gift.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ehh, none of us are interested in them. And if there's any chance of them leading you to the Mare Jivari, I'm sure an adventurer like you wouldn't want to pass on that opportunity.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Granny Itztli has a sense for these things.

dialogues.speaker: Leyla
dialogues.text: So, um, Granny Itztli... Do you think I'm still a spirit-duffer?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What kind of a dumb question is that? You saw through my illusion, didn't you? I mean, that's partly because I deliberately made it imperfect, but even then, a spirit-duffer wouldn't be able to see through that.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ororon, give this guy some lessons when you've got the time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Leyla, put in the work and we'll see how far you get.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Amazing... Life is so full of surprises. As long as you keep moving forward, you might just run into some fertilizer in the middle of the road.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm so happy for you, Leyla. Let's both give this our best shot, and who knows — we might both be beautiful cabbages one day.
